explanation: Pointing the soles of your feet at someone or propping your feet on furniture reads as careless or disrespectful in Germany, more a matter of posture and consideration for shared spaces than any belief about feet being unclean. It is a far milder issue than in cultures where feet carry a strong symbolic taboo.
local_tip: Keep both feet on the floor when sitting in company, especially in formal settings, and avoid resting your shoes on tables or chairs.

also_check.note: Feet are considered the lowest and most impure part of the body, so pointing them at people or at Buddha images is a serious offense.
Feet on furniture is often fine casually at home among family, but is considered inconsiderate in someone else's home or in formal settings.
Showing the soles of your feet is highly insulting, since feet are regarded as unclean and the gesture conveys contempt.

sources.title: Navigating German Etiquette: What Gestures Are Rude in Germany? - en.fmyly.com
